title: Stochastic quota harmonization with emergency circuit-breaker for limiter outages
creator: Aisha Romero
description:
Problem summary:

We have recurring incidents where regional quota controllers experience transient outages or large bursts that cause unfair token allocation and either excessive throttling or permissive behavior during reconciliation windows. Existing bucket-sync approaches create hard boundaries that amplify tail latency when cross-region failover happens, and our emergency fallback behavior is brittle: in some cases we over-provision (cost spike) or under-provision (customer errors and SLO violations).

This ticket proposes a new hybrid approach: 1) a stochastic token-bucket at the request router level to smooth bursts and probabilistically distribute short-term excess, 2) a time-decay reconciliation protocol for cross-region quota harmonization (reduces global thrashing), and 3) an emergency-tier circuit-breaker that activates a local degraded quota mode when the central limiter becomes unreachable. The goal is to preserve SLOs for critical tenants, improve fairness across short bursts, and ensure graceful degradation with clear observability and safety margins.
acceptance_criteria: New stochastic token-bucket implemented in the request ingress (perf < 2us added p50 on hotpath)
Cross-region reconciliation reduces quota oscillation metric (quota_delta_95) by >= 40% on synthetic burst tests
Emergency-tier circuit-breaker triggers within configured failure window and enforces degraded quotas with 100% audited decisions
No regressions on unit and integration tests; chaos test pass rate >= 95% for simulated region outage
Runbook and dashboard panels published to Console; alert thresholds defined and verified
implementation_notes: Ingress-layer stochastic bucket: use per-route lightweight PRNG to accept a fraction of burst tokens when bucket is exhausted (seeded by request hash to preserve session stickiness)
Time-decay reconciliation: each region publishes compact lease records (lease_ts, tokens_issued_decay) every 500ms; peers merge using exponential decay windows to avoid abrupt global state flips

Emergency-tier circuit-breaker: three-state (Closed, Degraded, Open). Degraded applies a local leaky-bucket derived from a conservative fraction of historical throughput for the tenant (configurable per-plan)
Telemetry: emit quota_decision_reason (local_bucket|stochastic_accept|reconciled_quota|degraded_cb) on each decision and surface counts to Console with per-tenant sankey view
Rollout: feature-flagged gated rollout by customer tier; start with internal-only tenants, then opt-in customers, then global default
design_tradeoffs: Stochastic accepts introduce non-determinism in acceptance which can make debugging harder; mitigated by deterministic seeding and comprehensive logging
Time-decay reconciliation favors stability over absolute correctness in short windows — small, transient quota imbalances are tolerated to avoid oscillation
Emergency-tier conservative quotas may reduce throughput for high-volume customers during outages. We prefer predictable degraded behavior over silent error spikes
rollout_plan: Week 1: Implement inbound stochastic bucket and feature-flag behind 'stochastic_quota_v1' (internal only)
Week 2: Add telemetry and unit tests; run load tests in perf lab for p95/p99 latency impact
Week 3: Implement cross-region reconciliation service and emergency-tier CB; integrate with Console panels
Week 4: Canary rollout to 5% of traffic (internal tenants + low-tier customers), monitor quota_delta_95 and decision-reasons
Week 5: Expand to 25% and run chaos test (region partition) to validate degraded behavior
Week 6: Global rollout to all hosted API traffic if metrics pass and no customer regressions
test_plan: Unit tests for probabilistic acceptance with deterministic PRNG seeds
Integration tests: multi-region emulation with synthetic bursts to validate reconciliation behaviour
Chaos tests: delay/partition central limiter, verify circuit-breaker transition and audit logs
Performance regression tests: ensure hotpath latency budget remains within 2us median impact
Customer canary with telemetry gating and automated rollback on SLO regressions
observability_and_metrics: SLO impact: user-visible error-rate, tail-latency for generation requests, and 99th token latency
cost metrics: token-cost delta during degraded mode
runbook_actions: If degraded_cb triggers for > 2 minutes: notify on-call, increase sampling of decision_reason, and consider rollback to previous limiter config
If reconciliation metrics show > 50% increase in quota oscillation: throttle reconcile frequency and widen decay window
For accidental over-accept (cost spike): immediately enable per-tenant emergency cap and run billing isolation
notes_and_discussion: 2026-03-02 (Aisha Romero): Initial spike analysis attached. Key observation: regional controller backlog correlates with aggressive global reconcile runs.
2026-03-04 (Priya Patel): PM feedback — must guarantee critical tenants (enterprise) are never dropped below minimal SLA during degraded mode
2026-03-06 (Liam Chen): Engineering review — prefer probabilistic approach over synchronized token borrowing due to lock contention risks
2026-03-08 (Security): no keys or secrets required for reconciliation; all lease records are signed and rate-limited
2026-03-09 (SRE): Add chaos scenario where background reconciliation messages are lost; verify no unbounded growth in accepted tokens
